newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities close higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities close higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities closed higher across the board on Monday in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.
"Government securities closed higher across the board on some speculative buying interest despite another hike in the interbank rate. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.60/2.50 percent compared with last Friday's yield of 2.53/2.48 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.60/2.50 percent against 2.57/2.52 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.60/98.70 from last Friday's close of S$98.53/98.58, May 2002 at S$99.60/99.70 versus S$99.55/99.60 and June 2003 at S$94.70/94.80 against S$94.65/94.70.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 1-7/8 1-3/4 percent from last Friday's 1-1/2 1-3/8 percent.
